issues.t: Collapsed lifter and worn camshaft on the 6.0L V8
issues.sym: A tapping or ticking from the engine that is louder when cold and does not go away, a rough idle or misfire, and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: The 6.0L V8 shuts off four cylinders to save fuel. The special lifters that do this can stick or collapse, and a failed lifter then chews up the camshaft lobe. GM issued service bulletins on lifter noise.
issues.next: Do not ignore a new ticking noise. Have it diagnosed soon; catching it early can mean replacing lifters before the camshaft or more of the engine is damaged.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch on the 3.6L V6
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam and crank timing codes such as P0011, P0014, P0021, P0024, P0016 or P0008, sometimes with a rattle on start-up or rough running.
issues.why: The timing chains on this V6 can stretch early, especially with long oil-change intervals, so the cam timing drifts out of range.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Change the oil on time with the right oil. A stretched chain should be replaced before it skips or breaks, which can wreck the engine.

issues.t: Front lower control arm clunk and worn ball joints
issues.sym: Clunking or rattling from the front over bumps, creaking when turning, a loose feel or shake under braking.
issues.why: The front lower control arms (also called tension struts) have bushings and ball joints that wear out early. This is the most reported G8 repair, and GM issued a service bulletin for it.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Badly worn ball joints are a safety risk, so do not wait long if a shop finds play.

issues.t: Oil pan gasket and rear main seal leaks
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, oil on the bottom of the engine or transmission bell housing, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The V8 oil pan gasket and rear main seal are frequent leak points; some pans were even porous.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and watch for drips. Have the source traced before replacing parts.

issues.t: Vibration in four-cylinder mode from worn engine mounts
issues.sym: A buzz or shake through the car while cruising when the V8 switches to four-cylinder mode.
issues.why: The 6.0L runs on four cylinders at light load, and worn or soft engine mounts let that vibration into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the engine and transmission mounts checked.

issues.t: Oil pressure sensor code P0521
issues.sym: Check engine light with P0521, or the oil pressure gauge jumps around.
issues.why: The oil pressure sender or its screen can fail or clog. GM issued bulletins for it. In rare cases a real low-pressure problem is behind the code.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. If the gauge drops to zero or you hear knocking, stop the engine right away. Otherwise have the sender and screen replaced.

issues.t: Engine computer failure (P0601) and reduced power
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0601, sudden reduced-power mode, or the engine shutting down.
issues.why: Several owners report the engine control module (ECM) failing internally or needing reprogramming.
issues.next: If the car drops into reduced power, get off the road safely. Have a shop confirm the ECM fault and try a software update before replacing it.

issues.t: Electronic throttle body failure
issues.sym: Check engine light and reduced power, or poor throttle response.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body can fail, and the computer limits power to protect the engine.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning sometimes helps, but a failed unit must be replaced.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: Battery or charging light, dim lights, a whining noise, or a dead battery.
issues.why: The alternator is one of the most common G8 electrical repairs; bearings and charging output fail.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. If the battery light is on, drive straight to a shop; the car may stall when the battery runs down.

issues.t: Harmonic balancer wobbles or fails
issues.sym: A wobbling crank pulley, belt squeal or chirp, or a vibration at idle.
issues.why: The rubber in the crank damper (harmonic balancer) can separate so the outer ring wobbles.
issues.next: Have it replaced soon; a failing balancer can throw the drive belt and damage the crank.

issues.t: A/C belt slips or comes off
issues.sym: Squeal, or the A/C stops cooling because the belt has come off.
issues.why: A separate A/C drive belt and its bracket or pulley can let the belt walk off. GM issued a bulletin for the bracket.
issues.next: Have the belt, tensioner and bracket checked.

issues.t: Automatic transmission flares, slips or shifts harshly
issues.sym: Engine revs flare between gears, harsh or late shifts, a slip, or limp mode.
issues.why: Owners report shift problems fixed by software updates, and some needed internal parts such as the front pump or a clutch pack.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about transmission software updates first, and have the fluid checked.

issues.t: Driveline vibration at highway speed
issues.sym: A vibration through the floor or steering wheel at highway speeds.
issues.why: Some cars needed the driveshaft re-indexed or replaced, or the driveshaft center bearing replaced.
issues.next: Have the wheels balanced first, then ask a shop to check the driveshaft.

issues.t: Instrument cluster or info display goes dark
issues.sym: The gauge cluster or driver information display stops working, so you lose the odometer, oil life and tire pressure readouts.
issues.why: The instrument cluster can fail internally.
issues.next: Get it fixed; you need working gauges and warning lights to drive safely. A rebuilt cluster is an option besides a new one.

issues.t: Fuel pump or fuel level sender failure
issues.sym: Cranks but will not start, stalls, a gas gauge that reads wrong, or a fuel smell.
issues.why: The G8 has a two-sided fuel tank with a pump and level senders that can fail.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, do not drive it. For a no-start, have fuel pressure checked.

issues.t: Door lock actuators fail
issues.sym: A door will not lock or unlock with the remote or switch, locks slowly, or the door will not latch.
issues.why: Door lock actuators and latch assemblies wear out or freeze.
issues.next: Have the affected door actuator replaced. A door that will not latch shut needs fixing right away.

issues.t: Front strut mounts knock or struts wear
issues.sym: Knocking or creaking from the front when turning or over bumps, or a bouncy ride.
issues.why: Upper strut mounts and bearings wear out early, and struts lose damping.
issues.next: Have the strut mounts and struts inspected along with the control arms.

issues.t: Sway bar end links clunk
issues.sym: A knock or clunk over small bumps at low speed.
issues.why: The sway bar end links and bushings wear and come loose.
issues.next: Have the links checked; they are a simple repair.

issues.t: ABS light from a broken rear wheel speed sensor wire
issues.sym: ABS and traction control lights come on.
issues.why: The wiring to the rear wheel speed sensors can break at the connector, or a sensor fails.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but ABS may not. Have the codes read and the sensor or harness repaired.

issues.t: Check engine light from the gas cap or EVAP system
issues.sym: A steady check engine light, often with codes P0455, P0442 or P0449.
issues.why: A gas cap that does not seal or a failed EVAP purge or vent solenoid lets fuel vapor escape. GM replaced caps under a bulletin.
issues.next: Tighten the gas cap until it clicks. If the light returns, have the EVAP system tested.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning faults
issues.sym: The tire pressure light stays on or the display shows dashes even when tires are full.
issues.why: Tire pressure sensor batteries die with age, and the receiver can fail.
issues.next: Check all tire pressures by hand first. Then have the sensors scanned and replaced as needed.

issues.t: Airbag light from the passenger seat sensor
issues.sym: The airbag light comes on, or the passenger airbag-off light behaves wrongly.
issues.why: The passenger seat occupant sensor or the airbag module can fail.
issues.next: Treat the passenger airbag as not working until it is fixed. Have the airbag codes read.

issues.t: Power window stops working
issues.sym: A window will not go up or down, works only sometimes, or streaks on the glass.
issues.why: Window motors, window control boards and wiring fail; some owners needed several repairs.
issues.next: If a window is stuck open, cover it and have the motor or switch diagnosed.

issues.t: Hood release cable breaks
issues.sym: The hood will not open when you pull the release.
issues.why: The hood release cable or latch can break.
issues.next: A shop can open the latch from underneath and replace the cable.

issues.t: Third brake light segments burn out
issues.sym: Part or all of the high-mounted center brake light stays dark.
issues.why: The LED segments in the center high-mounted stop lamp fail.
issues.next: Have it replaced; brake lights warn drivers behind you.

issues.t: Water leaks into the trunk
issues.sym: Damp carpet or water in the trunk.
issues.why: A failed wiring grommet or a door or window seal can let water in.
issues.next: Have the car water-tested to find the entry point, and dry it out to prevent mold and electrical damage.

issues.t: Front seat belt cable can break (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; the belt may not hold you in a crash.
issues.why: The cable for the front outboard seat belt tensioner can bend and break when people sit on it getting in. Recall 15V-399 fits a revised part.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Knee can knock the key out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can shut off if your knee hits the key fob while driving, which cuts power steering and power brakes and can stop the airbags from deploying.
issues.why: The flip key hangs where a driver's knee can bump it. Recall 14V-540 fits a revised key blade and housing.
issues.next: Until it is fixed, set the seat and steering wheel so your knee clears the key. Check your VIN and get the free repair.

issues.t: Brake lights may stay off and tire warning may be late (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights may not light when you brake, and the low tire pressure warning may not come on until pressure is very low.
issues.why: The brake pedal position sensor and the tire pressure settings were programmed wrong. Recall 09V-172 reprograms both.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights, and check your VIN for this recall.
